text:
maya: Heads up — while testing the Node quickstart sample app I hit a parity issue vs the documented curl example. SDK is silently dropping the `X-Client-TTL` header and also doing two background retries, which the REST example doesn't do. Repro below.

sam: can you paste the exact commands / snippet?

maya: sure. Node quickstart snippet:```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.text.generate({ model: 'gpt-neo-1', input: 'hello' });
```

curl that we use in docs:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" -H "X-Client-TTL: 30" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-1","input":"hello"}'
```

maya: when I run the curl I get 200 + single token stream. When I run the quickstart app I get a 200 but with an extra two retries from the SDK and server logs show `X-Client-TTL` is absent.

alex: hmm, SDK shouldn't mutate arbitrary headers. The quickstart client doesn't expose a way to pass custom headers AFAIK — are you adding headers anywhere?

maya: no. I expected the SDK to forward `X-Client-TTL` if I set it via `client.options.headers`. Tried `client.options.headers = { 'X-Client-TTL': '30' }` but server still logs it as missing.

lin: could be header normalization (underscore/case). Our server checks header name exact match? That would be a bug. Also curious about retries — what retry policy did you see?

maya: logs: `retry attempt 1, reason: ECONNRESET` then `retry attempt 2`. The REST curl had no ECONNRESET. The SDK is doing automatic retry with exponential backoff by default and not honoring `X-Client-TTL`.

sam: @maya can you share a small network dump or node fetch snippet so I can repro locally?

maya: attached paste (trimmed):```text
POST /v1/text/generate
Authorization: Bearer xxxx
User-Agent: redwood-sdk-node/0.9.1
Accept: application/json

# no X-Client-TTL header present
```

maya: another oddity — when I try the admin list endpoint from the sampleapp `client.admin.listModels()` it returns 404, but curl to `/v1/admin/models` returns 200. So there are at least two parity gaps: header forwarding and admin endpoints mapping.

alex: that suggests the SDK admin client might be hitting the wrong base path or using a different auth scope set. SDK default env var for admin basepath is `ADMIN_API_URL` fallback? We changed basepaths in the past.

lin: I glanced at the SDK code — `admin` methods currently call `/admin/v0/models` while server expects `/v1/admin/models`. Off by one version path. oof. That would explain the 404.

sam: good find. For the header thing, I suspect the SDK HTTP layer is sanitizing headers and dropping any headers starting with `X-Client-` unless specifically allowed (we whitelist a short list to avoid leaking internal headers). That would be on purpose but docs don't mention it — DX mismatch.

maya: yep, docs show `X-Client-TTL` as sample usage in quickstart though. Confusing for new users.

alex: action items: 1) sam to reproduce and open SDK GH issue for headers+retries (include minimal repro), 2) lin to confirm admin path version mismatch and propose patch, 3) update quickstart docs to note current header whitelist / or add an explicit API to set per-request headers.

sam: assigning to me. I can repro. Workaround for now: use `fetch` with curl-style headers or set `REDWOOD_SDK_DISABLE_AUTORETRY=1` env var to avoid the extra retries while we fix.

dev-ex-bot: Filed issue #584 in redwood-sdk-node: "Node SDK drops X-Client-* headers and uses v0 admin path causing 404; also default retry behavior differs from curl." <https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/584> 

maya: thanks. I'll add notes to the onboarding checklist so new users don't get blocked. Also adding a small code snippet to quickstart showing `fetch` fallback.

alex: +1. If lin's v0->v1 fix is trivial we should cut a patch release 0.9.2 and update docs.

lin: will PR today, include unit test for header passthrough and admin basepath.

sam: I'll paste repro steps into the issue and link the network dump.

maya: awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
